topics.title: Jaggery in Pickle: What Gor Does to Mango Achar
topics.excerpt: Why Gujarati kitchens use jaggery in mango pickle, how it changes flavour and colour, and how it differs from sugar.
topics.quick_answer: Jaggery (gor) adds a deep, caramel-like sweetness and a dark colour to mango pickle, and like sugar it helps preserve it. Gor Keri is the classic example: raw mango pieces in a thick jaggery masala.

list: A rounder, less sharp sweetness than white sugar.
Caramel and mineral notes.
A deep brown-red colour.
A thick syrup that coats the mango pieces.

p: Sugar gives a clean sweetness that lets mango sourness stand out — used in Chhundo and many Meethi Keri recipes. Jaggery gives a heavier, warmer sweetness that blends with mustard and chilli.
We do not claim jaggery makes pickle healthy; it is still a sweetener. The choice is about taste.
Jaggery syrup can thicken or crystallise in cool weather. That is natural — stir with a dry spoon.
Sweet syrups attract ants, so wipe the rim and close the lid firmly.

sections.h2: How jaggery goes into a pickle
p: Recipes differ, but the jaggery is usually either grated finely and mixed into the salted, drained mango with the masala, or melted gently into a syrup first. As it dissolves, it pulls moisture from the mango and forms a thick, dark coating around each piece.

Many traditional Gor Keri recipes then let the jar rest, sometimes in the sun, so the jaggery fully dissolves and the flavours blend. The result is a pickle where sweetness, sourness, and spice arrive together rather than one after another.

Because jaggery holds more moisture than sugar, cooks pay close attention to how dry the mango is before it goes in. Well-drained mango and fully dissolved jaggery give a thick, glossy pickle; wet mango can make the syrup thin and less stable.

sections.h2: Not all jaggery is the same
p: Most jaggery used in Gujarati pickles is made from sugarcane. Its colour ranges from pale gold to deep brown depending on how the juice is boiled and where the cane grows, and the flavour ranges from mild honey to strong molasses.

Darker jaggery gives a darker, more intense pickle; lighter jaggery gives a brighter, milder one. This is one reason Gor Keri from different homes — or even different batches — can look and taste slightly different.

Jaggery also absorbs moisture from the air, which is why good cooks store it dry and use it quickly once opened. The same care applies to a jaggery pickle: dryness keeps its syrup thick and its flavour clean for longer.

sections.h2: How jaggery works with pickle spices
p: Jaggery is especially good at rounding off bitter and pungent notes. Fenugreek, which can taste harsh on its own, becomes pleasantly bittersweet next to gor. Split mustard loses some of its sharpness, and red chilli feels warmer rather than sharper.

That is why jaggery pickles often feel less 'sweet' than sugar pickles with the same amount of sweetener: the jaggery blends into the spice rather than sitting on top of it. It suits people who find Chhundo too sweet but spicy keri achar too sharp.

On a Gujarati thali, Gor Keri usually plays the sweet-sour role opposite a spicy pickle. It is particularly useful beside spicy shaak, fried farsan, or kadhi-khichdi, where a little sweetness balances the meal.
Outside the thali, it pairs well with rotli and ghee, thepla, and bajra rotla, where it can even take the place of the plain lump of jaggery that is traditionally served alongside.
At festive meals, Gor Keri is often placed next to farsan such as dhokla, khaman, or fried snacks, where its sweet-sour taste cuts through oil in the same way a chutney would.

list: Jaggery colour and moisture differ from one batch of cane to the next.
Warm weather keeps the syrup loose; cold weather thickens it.
Over weeks, the mango releases more juice and the syrup darkens.
Crystals may form in cool weather; stirring with a dry spoon helps.
None of these changes on its own means the pickle has spoiled.

sections.h2: Jaggery and sugar side by side
list: Colour — jaggery gives brown to deep red-brown; sugar keeps the pickle golden or amber.
Flavour — jaggery tastes of caramel and molasses; sugar tastes clean and sweet.
Texture — jaggery syrup is usually thicker and more opaque; sugar syrup is glossier.
Pairing — jaggery suits rustic plates such as rotla and khichdi; sugar suits tea-time snacks such as khakhra and thepla.
Examples — Gor Keri uses jaggery; Chhundo typically uses sugar.

p: Sweet syrups attract ants and pick up moisture from the air more readily than oil does. Close the lid firmly after every use and wipe away any syrup on the rim or threads of the jar.

If you see the syrup crystallising in cold weather, do not add water to loosen it. Stir with a dry spoon, or let the jar sit somewhere warmer for a while. Adding water is one of the quickest ways to spoil a sweet pickle.

sections.h2: Who tends to enjoy jaggery pickles
p: Jaggery pickles often win over people who find spicy achar too sharp but sugar-based pickles too sweet. They are also popular with elders who grew up with gor on the plate at every meal, and with children who are just starting on pickle.
If you are unsure, try Gor Keri beside a spicy mango pickle for a week and notice which spoon you reach for with which dish.

Jaggery has a special place in Gujarati food. A small piece of gor is often served with the thali, and many everyday dishes — dal, kadhi, shaak — use a little jaggery to balance sour and spicy flavours. It is not surprising that the same instinct shaped pickles.

Gor Keri follows this logic. Rather than choosing between sweet and spicy, it uses jaggery to hold both together, which is why it feels at home on a Gujarati plate alongside dishes that are themselves gently sweet and sour.

For people who grew up outside Gujarat, Gor Keri can be a good introduction to that style of cooking. Taste it with a plain rotli first, then with dal-bhaat, and notice how the jaggery softens the chilli rather than hiding it.

faqs: Why is jaggery used in pickle?
For a deep, caramel-like sweetness and colour; it also helps preserve the pickle.
Is jaggery pickle healthier than sugar pickle?
We do not make health claims; both are sweeteners. Choose by taste.
Why does my jaggery pickle look crystallised?
Jaggery can crystallise in cool weather; it is natural.
Does jaggery pickle taste very sweet?
It is sweet, but jaggery blends with the spices, so many people find it less sugary than sugar-based pickles.
Why is Gor Keri darker than Chhundo?
Jaggery is naturally brown, while Chhundo uses white sugar, so Gor Keri is darker.
Can I use Gor Keri instead of jaggery on the thali?
Yes. Many people serve Gor Keri in place of a plain piece of gor, getting sweetness and sourness in one spoon.
Does jaggery pickle need the fridge?
Usually not. Keep it in a cool, dark cupboard with a tight lid; the fridge will thicken the syrup.
Is Gor Keri spicy?
It has gentle spice from chilli and mustard, but the jaggery softens it, so most people find it mild.
topics.conclusion: Jaggery gives Gor Keri its depth. If you like gur in your chai, you will likely prefer it to sugar-based sweet pickles.

topics.title: Salt and Turmeric in Achar: The First Step of Every Mango Pickle
topics.excerpt: Why every mango pickle begins with salt and turmeric, and what each does before the masala is added.
topics.quick_answer: Salt and turmeric are the first things added to cut raw mango. Salt draws out water and firms the pieces; turmeric gives colour and its traditional role in preservation. Only after this step and drying is the masala and oil added.

p: Raw mango is full of water. Rubbing the pieces with salt pulls that water out over several hours. The liquid is drained, and the pieces become firmer and more concentrated in flavour.
This step is why well-made pickle stays crisp. Skip it and the pickle becomes watery and spoils faster.
Turmeric is added with the salt. It gives mango pickle its golden base colour and has long been used in Indian kitchens as part of preserving vegetables.
We describe its culinary role only; we do not make medical claims.

list: Cut washed and dried raw mango.
Coat with salt and turmeric.
Rest, then drain the released liquid.
Dry the pieces, often in the sun.
Add masala and oil.

faqs: Why is salt added to mango pickle first?
To draw out water, firm the pieces, and help preserve the pickle.
Why is turmeric added to pickle?
For colour and its traditional role in preserving vegetables.
What happens if pickle has too little salt?
It can become watery and spoil faster.
topics.conclusion: Salt and turmeric do the quiet work that makes a pickle crisp and long-lasting.

topics.title: Hing in Pickle: Why a Pinch of Asafoetida Matters
topics.excerpt: What hing (asafoetida) does in Gujarati pickle, how much is used, and why it smells so strong in the tin.
topics.quick_answer: Hing (asafoetida) is used in small pinches in achar masala. Raw, it smells sharp and sulphurous; in oil and spices it mellows into a savoury, onion-garlic depth that rounds out mustard and fenugreek.

p: Hing is a dried resin from the roots of the Ferula plant, usually sold as a powder mixed with flour or gum. It is one of the most important background flavours in Gujarati and Jain cooking, where onion and garlic are often avoided.
A little goes a long way — too much makes a pickle bitter and medicinal.

list: Adds savoury depth without onion or garlic.
Softens the sharpness of raw mustard.
Balances fenugreek bitterness in methia pickles.
Gives the characteristic aroma when a jar is opened.

p: In a well-balanced pickle you will not taste hing as a separate flavour — you will notice that the pickle tastes fuller and more rounded. It is most noticeable in methi-based pickles like Chana Keri Methi.
If you are sensitive to hing, sweet pickles like Chhundo typically use little or none.

faqs: Why is hing used in pickle?
It adds savoury depth and balances mustard and fenugreek.
Does all pickle contain hing?
Many spicy Gujarati pickles do; sweet pickles often use little or none. Check the product page.
Why does hing smell so strong?
Raw hing is pungent; it mellows in oil and spices.
topics.conclusion: Hing is the pinch you do not notice until it is missing. It is part of why Gujarati achar tastes rounded.

topics.title: Groundnut Oil Pickle: Why Saurashtra Kitchens Use Peanut Oil
topics.excerpt: Why groundnut oil is the traditional pickle oil in Gujarat, how it differs from mustard oil, and what to look for on labels.
topics.quick_answer: Groundnut (peanut) oil is the traditional cooking and pickle oil of Saurashtra, one of India's major groundnut-growing regions. It has a mild, nutty taste that lets mango and spices lead, unlike the pungency of mustard oil used in North Indian achar.

p: Saurashtra grows a large share of India's groundnuts, and groundnut oil has long been the everyday cooking oil there. Pickles naturally use the oil the kitchen already trusts.
Cold-pressed or wood-pressed groundnut oil keeps more of its nutty aroma than refined oil.

sections.h2: Groundnut vs mustard oil in pickle
list: Groundnut — mild, nutty; spices and mango dominate. Common in Gujarati pickles.
Mustard — pungent, sharp; adds its own heat. Common in North and East Indian pickles.
Both form the protective oil layer that keeps air away.

p: A good label names the oil. 'Edible vegetable oil' tells you nothing. Our homepage describes our pickles as made with pure groundnut oil; each product page lists its ingredients.
Keep the pieces under the oil layer as packed — that layer is part of how the pickle keeps.

faqs: Why do Gujarati pickles use groundnut oil?
Saurashtra is a major groundnut region, and its mild, nutty oil lets spices and mango lead.
Is groundnut oil pickle safe for peanut allergy?
No. Anyone with a peanut allergy should avoid pickles made with groundnut oil.
Groundnut or mustard oil — which is better for pickle?
Neither is better; groundnut is milder and traditional in Gujarat, mustard is pungent and traditional in the north.
topics.conclusion: Groundnut oil keeps Gujarati pickle mild and nutty. If you have a peanut allergy, avoid it and check every label.

topics.title: White Layer on Pickle: Mould, Salt, or Oil? What to Do
topics.excerpt: Seeing a white film or spots on your pickle? How to tell mould from harmless salt or solidified oil — and when to throw it away.
topics.quick_answer: A fuzzy white, green, or grey growth is mould — discard the whole jar. A cloudy or solid layer in cold weather is usually oil that has thickened, and dry white crystals can be salt. When unsure, do not taste it.

list: Mould — fuzzy or cottony patches, sometimes green, grey, or black, often with a musty smell. Unsafe.
Solidified oil — cloudy, waxy layer in cold weather that melts back at room temperature. Harmless.
Salt crystals — dry, gritty white specks, usually near the rim. Harmless.

p: Do not scrape it off and eat the rest. Mould can spread invisibly through the pickle. Discard the whole jar.
Mould almost always starts from moisture — a wet spoon, water droplets from the lid, or pieces left above the oil layer.

list: Use only a completely dry spoon.
Keep pieces pressed under the oil.
Close the lid tightly after every use.
Store away from the sink, stove steam, and sunlight.
Wipe condensation from the lid in humid weather.

sections.h2: Checking a jar step by step
list: Look first without touching. Note the colour and texture of the layer and where it sits — on the surface, on the pieces, or near the rim.
Smell the jar. A spicy, mustard aroma is normal; a musty, damp, or alcoholic smell is not.
If the layer is cloudy and waxy and the room is cold, close the jar and leave it somewhere warmer for an hour. Oil that has thickened will clear.
If there are dry specks near the rim, check whether they are gritty — salt crystals feel like fine sand.
If anything looks fuzzy or cottony, stop. Do not stir it in, taste it, or scoop it out. Discard the jar.

p: Every cooking oil contains a mix of fats, and some of them start to solidify as the temperature drops. Groundnut oil in particular is known for turning cloudy or partly solid in cold weather or in the fridge. Mustard oil and other oils can also thicken.

The change is physical, not a sign of spoilage. The layer looks pale and waxy, has no fuzz, and melts back to clear oil at room temperature. If you store pickle in the fridge, expect this every time you take the jar out.
You can test this easily: move a cloudy jar to a warmer spot for an hour or two. If the layer disappears and the oil turns clear again, it was simply cold oil. Mould does not melt away with warmth.

list: The colour of the masala deepening over weeks.
Mango pieces gradually softening.
Masala settling at the bottom and oil rising to the top.
Sugar or jaggery syrup thickening or crystallising in the cold.
The aroma mellowing as the raw spice edge fades.

p: Some signs mean the pickle is spoiling even if you cannot see mould yet: bubbles or fizzing when you open the jar, a lid that bulges, a slimy coating on the pieces, or a sharp alcoholic or yeasty smell. These point to fermentation or microbial growth that should not happen in a properly stored oil pickle.
In all of these cases, discard the jar. Wash and dry the container completely before reusing it.

sections.h2: Protecting a jar once it is open
p: Most problems start in the first few centimetres of the jar, where pieces may poke above the oil and where moisture from the lid collects. After serving, press the pieces back down with a dry spoon so they sit under the oil.

Wipe the rim with a dry cloth before closing, especially with sweet pickles where syrup can gather. If you open the jar daily, consider decanting a week's worth into a small serving jar so the main jar stays closed.

Finally, trust your senses. A healthy pickle looks glossy, smells of mustard and spice, and has pieces that are firm or pleasantly soft. If a jar ever makes you hesitate, it is safer to throw it away than to taste it and find out.

sections.h2: Why mould appears in the first place
p: Mould needs moisture and air. A traditional oil pickle limits both: salt pulls water from the mango, and oil keeps air away from it. Mould usually appears where one of those defences has been broken.

The common causes are a spoon that was damp or had touched other food, condensation dripping from the lid, pieces sitting above the oil, or a jar kept near steam. In the monsoon, even opening the jar often in a humid kitchen can let in enough moisture over time.
Knowing the cause helps you protect the next jar. If mould appeared at the surface, the problem was likely the lid or exposed pieces; if it appeared deeper down, a wet spoon is the usual suspect.

sections.h2: What to do after discarding a jar
p: Empty the jar away from other food, then wash it in hot, soapy water, rinse well, and let it dry completely — ideally in sunlight for a few hours. Wash the lid, including any rubber seal, with equal care.
Check nearby jars as well, especially if they share a shelf that gets damp. Before opening the next jar, make sure your serving spoon is completely dry and set aside only for pickle.

Sweet pickles such as Chhundo, Meethi Keri, and Gor Keri can show different kinds of white or pale patches from oil pickles. Sugar crystals form in cool weather and look like small, hard, glittering grains, often around the rim or on the surface of the syrup. They dissolve when the jar warms up or when you stir with a dry spoon.

Mould on a sweet pickle looks the same as on any other food: soft, fuzzy, cottony growth, sometimes green or grey, usually with a damp smell. Sweet syrups draw moisture from the air, so a lid left loose in humid weather is a common cause.
As with oil pickles, if you are unsure whether you are looking at crystals or mould, do not taste. Crystals feel gritty and hard; mould is soft and fuzzy.

faqs: Is a white layer on pickle mould?
If it is fuzzy or has coloured spots, yes — discard the jar. A waxy layer in cold weather is usually thickened oil.
Can I remove mould and eat the rest?
No. Discard the whole jar.
Why did my pickle get mould?
Usually moisture from a wet spoon, lid condensation, or pieces above the oil.
Why does pickle oil turn white in the fridge?
Some fats in oil, especially groundnut oil, solidify in cold. The layer clears at room temperature and is harmless.
Is fizzing in pickle normal?
No. Fizzing or bubbles suggest fermentation or spoilage; discard the jar.
Can salt crystals form on pickle?
Yes. Dry, gritty white specks near the rim are often salt and are harmless.
Should I wash the lid if I see condensation?
Wipe it completely dry. If you wash it, make sure the lid and seal are fully dry before closing the jar.
topics.conclusion: Fuzzy means discard; waxy in winter means oil. A dry spoon prevents most problems.

topics.title: Should Pickle Be Refrigerated? Fridge vs Cupboard for Achar
topics.excerpt: Do Indian pickles need the fridge? When a cupboard is enough, when the fridge helps, and what to watch for.
topics.quick_answer: Traditional oil-cured Indian pickles usually keep well in a cool, dry cupboard and do not need refrigeration. A fridge can help in very hot, humid weather, but it may thicken the oil. Always follow the storage note on the jar.

sections.h2: Why most achar does not need the fridge
p: Salt, oil, spices, and drying are designed to keep pickle stable at room temperature. Indian homes stored pickles in barnis in storerooms for generations.
The real risks are moisture and heat, not room temperature itself.

list: Very hot, humid kitchens during monsoon.
Low-oil or low-salt pickles, if the label says so.
An open jar you will use slowly over many months.

p: Cold thickens oil and can make jaggery or sugar syrup stiff, so pickles look cloudy. Leave the jar out for a few minutes before serving.
Moving a jar in and out of the fridge causes condensation. If you refrigerate, keep it there and use a dry spoon.

list: Oil-cured mango pickles (keri achar, Katka Keri, Gunda Keri, Chana Keri Methi) — generally fine in a cool cupboard.
Sugar- or jaggery-based pickles (Chhundo, Meethi Keri, Gor Keri) — also usually fine at room temperature; the fridge will stiffen the syrup.
Water- or brine-based pickles — these contain more moisture and often need refrigeration.
Instant or fresh pickles such as quick carrot, radish, or green chilli pickles made for the week — refrigerate and use quickly.
Anything with a label instruction — the label wins over general advice.

sections.h2: Where to keep a jar in an Indian kitchen
p: The best spot is a closed cupboard away from the stove, the sink, and direct sunlight. Heat from cooking and steam from boiling pots both cause condensation inside the lid, which is one of the most common ways moisture reaches the pickle.

Avoid the top of the refrigerator, which is often warm from the motor, and windowsills, where sunlight heats the jar during the day. A lower shelf in a pantry or a storeroom is ideal — close to how barnis were kept in older homes.

If you have several jars, keep them together in one spot so you can see at a glance which one is open and which are sealed. Opening one jar at a time and finishing it before the next keeps every jar in its best condition.
Many families keep the main jar sealed in the cupboard and fill a small serving jar once a week. The main jar is opened rarely and only with a clean, dry spoon, so it stays protected for longer.

The small jar sits on the dining table or near the dabba and is used every day. If anything goes wrong — a wet spoon, a lid left open — only a small amount is affected. This habit works whether or not you use the fridge.
Choose a small glass or steel jar with a tight lid for serving, and wash and dry it completely before each refill. A clean, dry serving jar keeps the daily routine simple and protects the main jar.
In winter, oil-based pickles may look cloudy and sweet pickles may thicken even in the cupboard. That is simply the cold. Let the jar sit at room temperature before serving.

In peak summer, the main concern is heat. Keep jars low and away from walls that face the afternoon sun. If your kitchen is extremely hot and you use a jar slowly, the fridge is a reasonable choice as long as you keep the jar there consistently.

list: 'The fridge makes any pickle last forever.' It slows changes, but a wet spoon can still spoil a refrigerated jar.
'Cloudy oil means the pickle has gone bad.' Cold oil often turns cloudy and clears again at room temperature.
'Crystals in sweet pickle mean spoilage.' Sugar and jaggery can crystallise in cold; stir with a dry spoon.
'Room-temperature storage is unhygienic.' Traditional achar was designed for it; hygiene depends on dryness and a sealed lid.

sections.h2: How the fridge changes texture and flavour
p: Cold slows the maturing that makes pickle taste better over time. A jar kept in the fridge from the day it arrives will change more slowly — which some people like and others find flat. The masala may also taste muted straight from the fridge.

If you do refrigerate, take out only what you need a few minutes before the meal so the oil clears and the flavour opens up. Leaving the whole jar out repeatedly causes condensation, so it is better to spoon a portion into a small bowl and return the jar at once.

Oil-cured and sweet pickles are good travel companions because they do not need refrigeration for a journey. Pack the jar upright, with the lid tight and the jar wrapped so it cannot knock against other items.
When giving pickle as a gift, add a short note on storage: keep it in a cool, dark cupboard, use a dry spoon, and refrigerate only if the kitchen is very hot and the jar will be used slowly.

Before refrigerators were common, Indian families stored a full year of pickle in ceramic barnis kept in a cool storeroom. Jars were tied with cloth over the mouth, opened only with clean, dry hands or spoons, and often set out in the sun on dry days to drive off any moisture.
Those habits still hold up today. The main lessons — keep pickle cool, dark, and dry, and avoid bringing in moisture — matter more than whether the jar sits in a fridge or a cupboard.

Modern kitchens are often warmer and more humid than old storerooms, especially in apartments with little ventilation. That is why many families now use a mix of approaches: the main jar sealed in a cool cupboard, and a small serving jar used daily.

faqs: Do Indian pickles need to be refrigerated?
Most oil-cured pickles keep well in a cool, dry cupboard. Follow the jar's storage note.
Why does pickle look cloudy in the fridge?
Cold thickens the oil and sweet syrups; it clears at room temperature.
Is it bad to move pickle in and out of the fridge?
It can cause condensation; if you refrigerate, keep it there.
Do sweet pickles like Chhundo need the fridge?
Usually not. Sugar-based pickles keep in a cool cupboard; the fridge tends to stiffen the syrup.
Where should I not keep pickle?
Avoid spots near the stove, the sink, sunny windows, and the warm top of the refrigerator.
Can I keep pickle in the fridge door?
The door is the warmest, most frequently moved part of the fridge. A shelf inside is better if you refrigerate pickle.
Does refrigeration stop pickle from maturing?
It slows it down. A refrigerated jar changes flavour more slowly than one kept in a cupboard.
topics.conclusion: A cool, dry cupboard is enough for most achar. Use the fridge only in very humid heat, and then leave it there.

topics.title: Pickle in Monsoon: Keeping Achar Safe Through Humid Months
topics.excerpt: Monsoon humidity is hard on pickle. How to store jars, which habits prevent mould, and why pickle is a monsoon comfort food.
topics.quick_answer: Humidity is the main enemy of pickle in monsoon. Keep jars in the driest cupboard, use a dedicated dry spoon, wipe lid condensation, and decant small portions instead of opening the main jar at every meal.

sections.h2: Why monsoon is hard on pickle
p: In coastal Maharashtra and Gujarat, humidity stays high for months. Moisture condenses inside lids, spoons stay slightly damp, and cupboards near kitchens get warm and steamy.
Pickle does not spoil from the season itself; it spoils from moisture getting in.

list: Store jars away from the sink, stove, and outer walls that get damp.
Keep one spoon only for pickle and dry it fully after washing.
Decant a week's portion into a small dry bowl.
Check the lid for droplets and wipe them.
Keep pieces under the oil.

p: Rainy days mean khichdi, dal-bhaat, and bhajiyas — all better with a sharp pickle. Katka Keri and Gunda Keri suit khichdi; Chana Keri Methi goes well with hot bhajiyas and chai.
Buying 250 g jars in monsoon means each jar is finished before humidity becomes a problem.

faqs: How do I stop pickle getting mould in monsoon?
Keep jars dry and sealed, use a dry spoon, wipe lid condensation, and decant small portions.
Should I refrigerate pickle in monsoon?
It can help in very humid kitchens; if you do, keep it in the fridge.
Which pickle goes with monsoon khichdi?
Sharp, spicy pickles like Katka Keri or Gunda Keri.
topics.conclusion: Monsoon pickle care is about keeping moisture out. Smaller jars and a dry spoon make it easy.

topics.primary_keyword: why pickle has so much oil
topics.title: Why Does Pickle Have So Much Oil? The Role of the Oil Layer
topics.excerpt: The oil in achar is not excess — it protects the pickle. Why it is there, how much you should eat, and what to do with leftover oil.
topics.quick_answer: The oil layer in traditional pickle seals the mango and masala from air and moisture, which helps it keep for months without chemical preservatives. You do not need to eat the oil — lift pieces out and leave most of it in the jar.

list: Forms a seal over the pieces so air and moisture cannot reach them.
Carries the flavour of mustard, fenugreek, chilli, and hing.
Keeps the masala from drying out.
Slows oxidation that dulls colour and taste.

sections.h2: How to serve with less oil
p: Use a slotted spoon or press the pieces against the side of the jar before serving. The oil stays in the jar, protecting the rest of the pickle.
Keep the remaining pieces pushed down under the oil after each use.
When the pieces are finished, the spiced oil left behind is full of flavour. Many homes use a spoon of it to temper dal, mix into curd rice, brush on parathas, or toss with boiled potatoes.
Use it within a few weeks and only if it still smells fresh.

faqs: Why is there so much oil in pickle?
The oil seals the pickle from air and moisture, helping it keep for months.
Should I eat the pickle oil?
You do not have to; lift out the pieces and leave most oil in the jar.
What can I do with leftover pickle oil?
Use it to flavour dal, curd rice, parathas, or potatoes while it smells fresh.
topics.conclusion: The oil is protection, not excess. Serve pieces, leave the oil, and reuse what is left at the end.
